name: rice
soil: Heavy clay or clay loam with good water retention, pH 5.5–7.0

stages.name: Nursery
stages.description: Seeds germinated and seedlings raised in nursery beds.
stages.irrigation: Maintain 2–3 cm standing water in nursery after germination.
stages.fertilizer: Apply 1 kg Urea per 100 sq metre nursery area at 10 days.
tips: Transplant at 20–25 days when seedlings are 20–25 cm tall

stages.name: Transplanting / Early Vegetative
stages.description: Seedlings transplanted to puddled field. Roots establishing.
stages.fertilizer: Basal: 30 kg DAP + 20 kg MOP + 30 kg Urea per acre at transplanting.
watch_for: Dead heart caused by stem borer
tips: Plant 2–3 seedlings per hill, spacing 20 cm × 15 cm
Check for stem borer — cut affected tillers show dead heart

stages.name: Active Tillering
stages.description: Maximum tiller production. Green cover established.
stages.irrigation: Maintain 3–5 cm standing water. Drain field for 5–7 days mid-tillering to control unproductive tillers.
stages.fertilizer: Top dress 1: 25 kg Urea per acre at 30 days after transplanting.
tips: Monitor BPH weekly — colonies build fast
Do not apply excess Urea — promotes BPH and sheath blight

stages.name: Panicle Initiation / Booting
stages.description: Panicle forming inside flag leaf sheath. Most critical growth stage.
stages.irrigation: Maintain 5 cm standing water continuously — do not allow field to dry.
stages.fertilizer: Top dress 2: 20 kg Urea per acre at panicle initiation (PI stage).
watch_for: Blast disease on neck (neck blast — most damaging)
tips: Spray Tricyclazole 0.6 g/litre at PI stage for blast prevention
This stage determines final grain number — protect carefully

stages.name: Heading / Flowering
stages.irrigation: Maintain 3–5 cm water during heading and flowering.
tips: Avoid pesticides during flowering — kills pollinators
High temperature during flowering causes sterility

stages.name: Grain Filling / Ripening
stages.description: Grains fill with starch and ripen. Panicles turn golden.
stages.irrigation: Reduce water to 2–3 cm. Drain field 10–15 days before harvest.
watch_for: Rice bug (stink bug) sucking developing grains causing chalky spots
tips: Avoid delayed harvest — shattering losses increase

common_pests.name: Stem Borer
common_pests.symptoms: Dead heart in vegetative stage, white ear in reproductive stage
common_pests.control: Cartap hydrochloride 1.5 g/litre or Chlorantraniliprole 0.3 ml/litre

common_pests.name: Brown Plant Hopper (BPH)
common_pests.symptoms: Circular patches of burnt plants (hopper burn), insects at base
common_pests.control: Buprofezin 1 ml/litre — do NOT use pyrethroids (causes resurgence)

common_pests.name: Leaf Folder
common_pests.symptoms: Leaves rolled into tubes, white streaks

common_diseases.name: Blast
common_diseases.symptoms: Diamond-shaped grey lesions with brown border on leaves; brown neck at panicle base

common_diseases.name: Sheath Blight
common_diseases.symptoms: Oval water-soaked lesions on sheath, white with brown border

common_diseases.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB)
common_diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked stripe on leaf margins turning yellow then white
common_diseases.control: Spray copper oxychloride 3 g/litre; no curative chemical — use resistant varieties
